name: Electroscope
desc: A device that detects electric charge, starting with Gilbert's pivoted-needle versorium; later gold-leaf versions measured it.

name: Electrostatic generator
desc: A friction machine that builds up static charge, first Guericke's sulfur globe; it made electricity available for experiment.

name: Leyden jar
desc: A glass jar lined with metal foil that stores static charge; the first capacitor.

name: Coulomb's law
desc: The inverse-square law of force between electric charges, measured with a torsion balance.

name: Arc lamp
desc: Light from an electric arc between carbon rods, the first electric light, used for streets and lighthouses.

name: Galvanometer
desc: A needle deflected by a current-carrying coil, the first instrument to detect and measure electric current.

name: Thermocouple
desc: Two dissimilar metals joined to produce a temperature-dependent voltage (Seebeck effect); a basic temperature sensor.

name: Ohm's law
desc: The proportional relation between voltage, current and resistance that underlies circuit design.

name: Faraday's law of induction
desc: A changing magnetic flux induces a voltage in a conductor; the basis of generators, transformers and inductors.

name: Inductor
desc: A coil that stores energy in its magnetic field and resists changes in current; a basic passive component.

name: Commutator
desc: A rotary switch that reverses current in a machine's windings, enabling DC motors and generators.

name: Relay
desc: An electromagnetically operated switch that lets a small current control a larger one; key to telegraphy and switching.

name: Induction coil
desc: A transformer with an interrupter that turns low-voltage DC into high-voltage pulses for sparks and discharge tubes.

name: Resistor
desc: A component that sets a fixed opposition to current, used to control voltages and currents in circuits.

name: Potentiometer
desc: A resistor with a sliding contact, used to measure voltage and as an adjustable divider or control knob.

name: Wheatstone bridge
desc: A balanced four-arm circuit that measures an unknown resistance precisely.

name: Kirchhoff's circuit laws
desc: Conservation rules for current at nodes and voltage around loops, the foundation of circuit analysis.

name: LC circuit
desc: A capacitor and inductor that oscillate at a resonant frequency; the tuning element of radio.

name: Geissler tube
desc: A sealed low-pressure gas tube that glows when high voltage is applied; ancestor of neon and fluorescent lamps.

name: Self-excited dynamo
desc: A DC generator whose own output energizes its field magnets, making large-scale electric power practical.

name: Crookes tube
desc: A high-vacuum discharge tube in which cathode rays were studied, leading to X-rays and the electron.

name: Gramme machine
desc: A ring-armature dynamo giving smooth, high DC output; the first commercially successful generator.

name: Photoconductivity
desc: Discovery that selenium's resistance drops in light, the first light-sensitive electronic effect.

name: Capacitor
desc: Compact paper-and-foil and later film capacitors that store charge and filter signals in circuits.

name: Hall effect
desc: A voltage across a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field; later used to sense fields and probe semiconductors.

name: Piezoelectricity
desc: The Curie brothers' discovery that some crystals produce voltage under stress and deform under voltage.

name: Thermionic emission
desc: Electrons boiling off a heated filament (the Edison effect), the principle behind vacuum tubes.

name: Ammeter
desc: A calibrated instrument for measuring current; the moving-coil design made it rugged and accurate.

name: Alternator
desc: A generator that produces alternating current directly, used in AC power systems.

name: Alternating current
desc: Current that reverses direction periodically, easily stepped up or down by transformers for long-distance power.

name: Photoelectric effect
desc: Emission of electrons from metals struck by light, observed by Hertz and later explained by Einstein.

name: Polyphase system
desc: Multiple AC currents offset in phase, which produce rotating magnetic fields and efficient power transmission.

name: Induction motor
desc: A brushless AC motor driven by a rotating magnetic field; the workhorse of industry.

name: Synchronous motor
desc: An AC motor that turns in exact step with the supply frequency, used for clocks and large drives.

name: Liquid crystal
desc: A state of matter between liquid and solid whose molecular alignment can be switched; the basis of LCDs.

name: Voltmeter
desc: An instrument that measures electric potential difference, built from a galvanometer and series resistor.

name: Tesla coil
desc: A resonant air-core transformer producing very high-voltage, high-frequency alternating current.

name: Wireless power transfer
desc: Transmitting electrical energy without wires, from Tesla's demonstrations to modern inductive phone chargers.

name: Chemical vapor deposition
desc: Depositing thin solid films from reacting gases; first used for lamp filaments, later central to chipmaking.

name: Phototube
desc: An evacuated tube with a light-sensitive cathode that converts light into current.

name: Electrolytic capacitor
desc: A capacitor using a thin anodized oxide film as dielectric, giving large capacitance in a small volume.

name: Mercury-vapor lamp
desc: A gas-discharge lamp exciting mercury vapor, efficient for streets and the precursor of fluorescent tubes.

name: Heterodyne
desc: Mixing two frequencies to produce new sum and difference frequencies, proposed by Fessenden.

name: Mercury-arc valve
desc: A mercury-pool rectifier that converted high-power AC to DC for railways and industry.

name: Triode
desc: De Forest's Audion added a control grid to the vacuum diode, making the first electronic amplifier.

name: Crystal detector
desc: A point contact on a mineral crystal that rectifies radio signals; the first semiconductor device.

name: Electroluminescence
desc: Light emitted by a material when current passes through it, first seen by Round in silicon carbide.

name: Neon lighting
desc: Glass tubes filled with neon or other gases that glow brightly, used for signs.

name: Seven-segment display
desc: Seven bars arranged to form any digit, the standard layout for numeric readouts.

name: Electronic amplifier
desc: A circuit that boosts a signal's power, first with triodes; it made long-distance telephony and radio practical.

name: Regenerative circuit
desc: Armstrong's positive-feedback receiver that greatly increased triode gain and sensitivity.

name: Electronic oscillator
desc: A circuit that generates a steady periodic signal, the source of carrier waves and clocks.

name: Czochralski method
desc: Pulling a single crystal from a melt; adapted in 1950 to grow the silicon and germanium for transistors.

name: Neon lamp
desc: A small glow lamp with two electrodes in neon, used as indicators and voltage references.

name: Flip-flop
desc: Eccles and Jordan's two-state trigger circuit that stores one bit; the basis of digital memory and counters.

name: Superheterodyne receiver
desc: Armstrong's receiver that converts signals to a fixed intermediate frequency, the design of nearly all radios since.

name: Multivibrator
desc: A two-stage switching circuit that oscillates, triggers or holds state; a basic timing building block.

name: Tetrode
desc: A vacuum tube with a screen grid that cuts grid-anode capacitance, allowing higher frequency gain.

name: Stepper motor
desc: A motor that moves in precise discrete steps, used for positioning in printers and machines.

name: Crystal oscillator
desc: An oscillator stabilized by a vibrating quartz crystal, the precise timebase in clocks, radios and computers.

name: Power inverter
desc: A device that converts DC into AC, now built with transistors for solar systems and motor drives.

name: Field-effect transistor concept
desc: Lilienfeld's idea of controlling a semiconductor's conductivity with an electric field, realized decades later.

name: Pentode
desc: A tube with a suppressor grid that removes the tetrode's secondary-emission kink, the standard amplifier tube.

name: Ceramic capacitor
desc: A small, cheap capacitor with a ceramic dielectric; multilayer versions are the most common component made.

name: Negative-feedback amplifier
desc: Black's amplifier that feeds back part of its output to cut distortion and stabilize gain.

name: Thyratron
desc: A gas-filled tube used as a high-power controlled switch, a precursor of the thyristor.

name: Van de Graaff generator
desc: A belt-charged electrostatic machine reaching millions of volts, used in early particle accelerators.

name: Ferrite core
desc: Ceramic magnetic oxides with low losses at high frequency, used in inductors, transformers and antennas.

name: Thermistor
desc: A semiconductor resistor whose resistance changes strongly with temperature, used for sensing and protection.

name: Photoresistor
desc: A cadmium sulfide or similar cell whose resistance falls with light, used in light meters and switches.

name: Oscilloscope
desc: An instrument that draws voltage against time on a screen, the essential tool for seeing electronic signals.

name: Sodium-vapor lamp
desc: A very efficient discharge lamp with a yellow glow, widely used in street lighting.

name: Phase-locked loop
desc: A feedback system that locks an oscillator to a reference phase, used in tuning, clocks and demodulation.

name: Selenium rectifier
desc: A metal-semiconductor rectifier stack that was a common solid-state power rectifier before silicon diodes.

name: Differential amplifier
desc: An amplifier of the difference between two inputs that rejects common noise; the core of op-amps.

name: Schmitt trigger
desc: A comparator with hysteresis that turns noisy signals into clean digital transitions.

name: Photomultiplier tube
desc: A phototube with a chain of electron-multiplying dynodes that can detect single photons.

name: Waveguide
desc: A hollow metal pipe that guides microwaves with low loss, essential for radar and microwave links.

name: Printed circuit board
desc: Eisler's etched copper wiring on an insulating board, which made electronics compact and mass-producible.

name: Klystron
desc: A velocity-modulated tube that amplifies microwaves, used in radar, broadcasting and particle accelerators.

name: Fluorescent lamp
desc: A mercury discharge tube coated with phosphor that converts ultraviolet into visible light efficiently.

name: Schottky diode
desc: A metal-semiconductor junction diode with low forward drop and fast switching.

name: Strain gauge
desc: A resistive foil or wire whose resistance changes with stretch, used to measure force and weight.

name: Cavity magnetron
desc: A tube generating high-power microwaves in resonant cavities, which made compact radar and microwave ovens possible.

name: Semiconductor doping
desc: Adding trace impurities to a semiconductor to control whether it carries electrons or holes.

name: p–n junction
desc: The boundary between p- and n-type semiconductor, discovered by Ohl; the basis of diodes, transistors and solar cells.

name: Operational amplifier
desc: A high-gain DC amplifier configured by feedback to add, integrate or filter; later the most common analog IC.

name: Traveling-wave tube
desc: A broadband microwave amplifier tube still used in satellite transponders and radar.

name: Point-contact transistor
desc: Bardeen and Brattain's first working transistor, two gold contacts on germanium.

name: Zener diode
desc: A diode designed to conduct in reverse at a set voltage, used as a voltage reference and regulator.

name: Photodiode
desc: A p–n junction that converts light into current, used in optical sensing and communication.

name: Bipolar junction transistor
desc: Shockley's sandwich transistor of p- and n-layers, the mainstay of early solid-state electronics.

name: Zone melting
desc: Pfann's method of purifying crystals by sweeping a molten zone, which produced ultrapure germanium and silicon.

name: Avalanche photodiode
desc: A photodiode with internal gain from avalanche multiplication, used in fiber optics and lidar.

name: JFET
desc: The junction-gate field-effect transistor, the first practical FET.

name: Analog-to-digital converter
desc: A circuit that turns continuous voltages into numbers, linking the physical world to digital processing.

name: Nixie tube
desc: A neon glow tube with stacked digit-shaped cathodes, the standard numeric display before LEDs.

name: Thyristor
desc: A four-layer silicon switch (SCR) that latches on, replacing mercury-arc valves in power control.

name: Supercapacitor
desc: A double-layer capacitor with very high capacitance that bridges capacitors and batteries.

name: Thermal oxidation of silicon
desc: Growing a protective silicon dioxide layer on silicon, which passivated surfaces and masked diffusion.

name: Tunnel diode
desc: Esaki's heavily doped diode that uses quantum tunneling for very fast switching.

name: Wire bonding
desc: Connecting a chip to its package with fine gold or aluminium wires.

name: Halogen lamp
desc: An incandescent lamp with halogen gas that redeposits tungsten, giving brighter, longer-lived light.

name: Switched-mode power supply
desc: A supply that switches rapidly and filters the result, far more efficient and compact than linear supplies.

name: Planar process
desc: Hoerni's method of building transistors under a flat oxide layer, which made monolithic integrated circuits manufacturable.

name: MOSFET
desc: Atalla and Kahng's metal-oxide-semiconductor transistor, the most manufactured device in history.

name: Epitaxy
desc: Growing a crystalline layer aligned with a substrate, giving controlled device layers.

name: Brushless DC motor
desc: A motor commutated electronically rather than by brushes, used in drives, fans and drones.

name: Light-emitting diode
desc: A diode that emits light when current flows; Holonyak's red LED of 1962 began solid-state lighting.

name: Laser diode
desc: A semiconductor laser in a p–n junction, now used in fiber optics, optical discs and barcode readers.

name: Thin-film transistor
desc: A transistor deposited as thin films on glass, used to drive pixels in flat-panel displays.

name: CMOS
desc: Complementary pairs of n- and p-type MOSFETs that draw power only when switching; the basis of nearly all modern chips.

name: Transistor-transistor logic
desc: A bipolar logic family that became the standard building block of digital systems in the 1960s and 1970s.

name: Opto-isolator
desc: An LED and photodetector in one package that pass signals while electrically isolating circuits.

name: SRAM
desc: Memory holding each bit in a transistor latch, fast and used for processor caches.

name: Dual in-line package
desc: The rectangular chip package with two rows of pins, standard for decades.

name: Flip chip
desc: Mounting a die face down on solder bumps for short, dense connections.

name: Plasma display
desc: A panel of tiny gas cells glowing like neon lamps, used for early terminals and large flat TVs.

name: Moore's law
desc: Moore's observation that transistor counts per chip double regularly, which guided the industry for decades.

name: Hall effect sensor
desc: A semiconductor sensor that measures magnetic fields, used for position, speed and current sensing.

name: Surface-mount technology
desc: Soldering components directly onto board surfaces instead of through holes, enabling small, automated assembly.

name: Touchscreen
desc: A display that senses a finger's position; Johnson's capacitive design came first.

name: Self-aligned gate
desc: Using the gate itself as a mask for source and drain doping; with silicon gates it made MOS chips fast and dense.

name: Vacuum fluorescent display
desc: A phosphor-coated anode display lit by electrons from a filament, common in calculators and appliances.

name: Floating-gate MOSFET
desc: A MOSFET with an isolated gate that traps charge for years, the storage cell of nonvolatile memory.

name: MEMS
desc: Microscopic mechanical structures made with chip fabrication methods, used in sensors and actuators.

name: Variable-frequency drive
desc: Electronics that vary supply frequency to control AC motor speed, saving large amounts of energy.

name: Molecular-beam epitaxy
desc: Growing crystals one atomic layer at a time in ultra-high vacuum, enabling quantum wells and HEMTs.

name: Liquid-crystal display
desc: A flat display that switches liquid crystals with voltage to modulate light; low power and thin.

name: Charge-coupled device
desc: A chip that shifts packets of charge between cells, the first practical solid-state image sensor.

name: Ion implantation
desc: Firing accelerated dopant ions into silicon for precise, uniform doping.

name: DRAM
desc: Memory storing each bit as charge on a capacitor with one transistor; the main memory of computers.

name: EPROM
desc: Erasable programmable read-only memory, wiped by ultraviolet light through a quartz window.

name: Resistive touchscreen
desc: Hurst's two conductive layers that register touch where they are pressed together.

name: Active-matrix LCD
desc: An LCD with a transistor at each pixel, enabling laptop screens and flat-panel TVs.

name: Reactive-ion etching
desc: Plasma etching that cuts vertical features precisely, enabling ever-smaller chip patterns.

name: Dennard scaling
desc: The rule that shrinking MOSFETs keeps power density constant, which drove chip speed gains until about 2006.

name: Atomic layer deposition
desc: Depositing films one atomic layer per cycle with self-limiting reactions, vital for high-k gates and 3D memory.

name: Electronic paper
desc: Reflective displays that mimic ink on paper and hold an image without power, used in e-readers.

name: Power MOSFET
desc: A MOSFET built to switch large currents quickly, the basis of efficient power supplies.

name: EEPROM
desc: Electrically erasable programmable memory that can be rewritten in circuit.

name: Wafer stepper
desc: A lithography machine that exposes a chip pattern repeatedly across a wafer with reduction optics.

name: High-electron-mobility transistor
desc: A heterojunction FET with very fast electrons; in gallium nitride it became a key RF and power device.

name: Compact fluorescent lamp
desc: A folded fluorescent tube with an electronic ballast that fits standard bulb sockets.

name: Quantum dot
desc: Nanocrystals whose emission color depends on size, used in displays and imaging.

name: IGBT
desc: A MOS-gated bipolar power switch that handles high voltage efficiently; key to electric trains, EVs and inverters.

name: Excimer laser lithography
desc: Deep-ultraviolet lithography with excimer lasers, which carried chip scaling for decades.

name: Multi-touch
desc: Sensing several touches at once, enabling pinch and swipe gestures on phones and tablets.

name: Flash memory
desc: Masuoka's block-erasable floating-gate memory, later stacked into 3D NAND; the storage in phones and SSDs.

name: Projected capacitive touchscreen
desc: A grid of electrodes that senses the capacitance of fingers through glass, standard on smartphones.

name: Chemical-mechanical polishing
desc: Flattening wafers with abrasive slurry and chemistry, making many-layer wiring possible.

name: Digital micromirror device
desc: A chip with millions of tilting mirrors that forms images in DLP projectors.

name: OLED
desc: Tang and VanSlyke's organic light-emitting diode, thin emissive layers that need no backlight.

name: Giant magnetoresistance
desc: Large resistance changes in magnetic multilayers, which enabled high-density hard-disk read heads and spintronics.

name: FinFET
desc: A transistor whose channel is a vertical fin wrapped by the gate; mass-produced from 2011 to keep scaling going.

name: Ball grid array
desc: A package with solder balls across its underside, allowing hundreds of connections.

name: Blue LED
desc: Bright gallium nitride blue LEDs by Akasaki, Amano and Nakamura, which made white LED lighting possible.

name: CMOS image sensor
desc: An image sensor with an amplifier in each pixel, made in standard CMOS; the camera in every phone.

name: MEMS gyroscope
desc: A tiny vibrating structure that senses rotation through the Coriolis effect, used in phones, cars and drones.

name: Tunnel magnetoresistance
desc: Spin-dependent tunneling through a thin insulator, used in disk heads and magnetic memory.

name: White LED lamp
desc: Blue LEDs with yellow phosphor that produce white light, now replacing most incandescent and fluorescent lamps.

name: Copper interconnect
desc: Replacing aluminium chip wiring with lower-resistance copper using damascene polishing.

name: Silicon on insulator
desc: Building transistors on a thin silicon layer over oxide to cut leakage and capacitance.

name: MicroLED
desc: Arrays of microscopic inorganic LEDs forming pixels, offering bright, durable emissive displays.

name: SiC and GaN power devices
desc: Silicon carbide and gallium nitride switches that run hotter, faster and more efficiently than silicon, used in EV chargers and inverters.

name: AMOLED
desc: OLED displays driven by thin-film transistors, used in most high-end phones.

name: Immersion lithography
desc: Lithography through a water layer to sharpen resolution, used to print features below 50 nm.

name: MRAM
desc: Nonvolatile memory storing bits in magnetic tunnel junctions, fast and durable.

name: Through-silicon via
desc: Vertical copper connections through a silicon die that let chips be stacked.

name: High-k metal gate
desc: Replacing silicon dioxide gate insulators with hafnium oxide to stop leakage at small sizes.

name: Memristor
desc: A resistor whose value remembers past current, demonstrated in titanium oxide and studied for memory and neural hardware.

name: Quantum dot display
desc: Displays using quantum dots to convert backlight into pure colors for wider color range.

name: High Bandwidth Memory
desc: Stacked DRAM dies linked by through-silicon vias beside a processor, crucial for GPUs and AI accelerators.

name: Chiplet
desc: Building a processor from several smaller dies in one package, improving yield and mixing process nodes.

name: EUV lithography
desc: Lithography with 13.5 nm light from tin plasma and mirror optics, used in volume production from 2019.

name: Gate-all-around FET
desc: Transistors whose gate surrounds stacked nanosheet channels, in mass production from 2022 at the 3 nm node.
